title: The Fourier–Deligne transform
statement:
With $\Lambda$, $\pi:V\to S$, $\pi':V'\to S$, $b$, $\Psi$ and the kernel
$\mathcal K_\psi$ of [sk-def-kernel], let $p_1:V\times_SV'\to V$ and
$p_2:V\times_SV'\to V'$ be the projections, assume $p_2$ admits a
compactification, and let $r\in\mathbf Z$. The *Fourier–Deligne transform*
is the functor between the derived categories of étale sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules

$$
\FT_\psi:D(V_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)\to D(V'_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda),\qquad
\FT_\psi(K):=Rp_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)[r],
$$

$\mathcal K_\psi$ being placed in degree $0$. In the application $V_0\to S_0$
is a vector bundle of rank $r$ and $V'=V_0^\vee$ (Laumon's normalization);
the transform with the inverse character is the same construction with
$\Psi^{-1}$ in place of $\Psi$. On $\Aone$ one has $r=1$ and
$\FT_\psi(K)=Rp_{2,!}(p_1^*K\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi)[1]$.

lean.statement: def sfWeilFourierTransformObj (F : FourierSetting.{u}) (Ψ : AddChar (ZMod F.field.p) F.coefficients.Qbar) (c : Compactification (sfFourierSnd F).left) (K : sfCommonStageWeilComplex F.field F.coefficients.l F.coefficients.different (sfFourierLine F) F.coefficients.Qbar) : sfCommonStageWeilComplex F.field F.coefficients.l F.coefficients.different (sfFourierLine F) F.coefficients.Qbar
lean.note: The recorded closed audit points to AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.fourierTransform in WeilConjectures.FourierTransform.Defs: this is the exact general ordinary-etale definition but cannot take the actual common-stage adic Weil pairs used by sk-def-trace. It is retained by public import and lean.declarations. The added specialization constructs the rank-one Fourier object on precisely sfCommonStageWeilComplex using the published completed Artin-Schreier kernel, its canonical arithmetic-descent Weil map, the normalized completed pullback/tensor comparison, and zlComplexShriek with its canonical Frobenius mates. The shift [1] is moved into the kernel by the usual tensor and compact-support shift identifications. No arbitrary map, extra coefficient assumption, or replacement category is used. Every helper belongs to this Fourier construction; the module adds no independent notion.
